diagnosis.root_cause: The all-PONs-failed alarm is a false critical caused by failure of the OLT PON OID subtree/live PON probe, not by an actual OLT or PON outage. The OLT management plane remains reachable and healthy, and subscriber service is demonstrably active.
evidence: The trigger reports all 7 PONs failed simultaneously, which is inconsistent with the subscriber and historical service evidence.
The OLT responds to ping and general SNMP, while only the PON OID subtree fails; this isolates the problem to PON telemetry/probing rather than total OLT failure.
OLT CPU is 22%, memory is 19%, temperature is 44C, and uptime is stable, all close to healthy baselines.
The affected subscriber is currently stored as online with RX -19.84 dBm and TX 2.29 dBm, both normal; seven-day optical readings are stable and distance remains constant at 142 m.
The subscriber has normal authentication activity: 2 sessions in 24 hours, 15 in 7 days, and an average duration of 694 minutes, with a current assigned IP.
RADIUS data, CRM data, line ID, MAC, and assigned IP are consistent, ruling out an authentication or provisioning fault.
The router is reachable with an OK heartbeat, low CPU, and normal temperature, and the expected customer VLAN 1022 is present.
Only 9 of 183 ONUs are offline, below the expected background level for this population, so there is no evidence of an OLT-wide customer outage.
All live ONU probes return null values because the PON subtree is unavailable; null readings must not be interpreted as optical failures.
The customer and port traffic remain active, further confirming that the critical all-PON failure indication is monitoring-related.

remediation.action: Suppress or clear the false alarm after validating the OLT PON subtree and monitoring collector. Check SNMP view/permissions, OID compatibility with firmware V2.04.12R, SNMP timeouts, and the health-check implementation; restart or repair the monitoring poller if appropriate. Re-run per-PON probes and verify ONU online states before escalating to field work. Do not replace the OLT or dispatch for fibre faults based on this alarm alone.

ground_truth.root_cause: The OLT firmware (V2.04.12R) does not expose the ONU parameter OID subtree the health check reads. Every sampled ONU returns no instance, the check marks all seven PONs failed and writes a critical status, while the OLT and all 183 customers are operating normally.
expected_reasoning: Health check reports critical with all 7 of 7 PONs failed
OLT ping succeeds and SNMP sysUpTime answers, with 61 days of uptime and no recent reboot
OLT CPU 22%, memory 19% and temperature 44C are all at healthy baseline
Live probe returns oid_subtree_responds false, and every ONU on the port returns responds false rather than online 0
Uniform non-response means nothing answered; it is not a definite negative, so no ONU has been reported down
CRM shows 174 of 183 ONUs online, and 9 offline matches the 4.85% network baseline
The representative customer holds a session opened 14 hours ago and is passing normal daily traffic
Cached optical readings are 22 minutes old and normal, and telemetry has been flat for seven days
Healthy service with uniform probe non-response indicates an OID or firmware mismatch in the monitoring tool, not a network outage

expected_escalation.review_reason: Health check produces false criticals on firmware V2.04.12R; the OID subtree it reads is absent on this version

distractors: The critical alarm invites an olt_failure or pon_port_failure diagnosis
Nine genuinely offline ONUs on the OLT are unrelated background noise at the normal rate
Firmware V2.04.12R differs from the estate norm V2.03.78R, which is the discriminator rather than a fault in itself
